finding: The grounding layer's honest line landed on ORDINARY CONVERSATION. 'No advice, I just need to vent for a second...' classified CORRECTION (the '^no[,\s]' pattern), and "My dad has tests tomorrow. He's being casual about it." classified INSTRUCTION (the contracted pronoun "he's" was not in the non-imperative opener set, so the fragment read as a command about "it"). Both then read as requesting a mutation, and the reply to each had 'On that last change specifically: nothing was written' appended to it. This is the single worst class of defect for the original complaint: machinery intruding on a vent and a disclosure about David's father.

implementation: Three fixes: a contracted pronoun is still a pronoun (contraction tail stripped before the opener check); 'No,' opens a correction only when it contradicts something; and a CORRECTION only counts as REQUESTING a change when it carries a value or a contrast ('not X', 'instead', a digit, a quoted value) — belt and braces, so a misclassification alone cannot reach the grounding check. Also: an uninflected-verb check and a 3-word minimum, so 'Looks embarrassed about it.' and 'One leaf.' are no longer imperatives.
